name: wildcard-repeated-reference
desc: multiple references to the same wildcard-imported declaration
code: import package::other::*; const result = x + x;
result: const package_other_x = 1u; const result = package_other_x + package_other_x;

name: wildcard-collection
desc: a nested import collection can combine a wildcard with an explicitly imported item
code: import package::outer::{y, inner::*}; const result = x + y;
result: const package_outer_inner_x = 1u; const package_outer_y = 2u; const result = package_outer_inner_x + package_outer_y;

name: wildcard-shadow
desc: local declaration shadows a wildcard import
code: import package::other::*; var<private> x: f32 = 0; fn f() { x++; }
result: var<private> x: f32 = 0; fn f() { x++; }

name: wildcard-block-shadow
desc: an inner block shadows the wildcard, but the outside reference is unaffected
code: import package::other::*; fn f() -> u32 { { let x = 2u; } return x; }

name: wildcard-import-shadow
desc: an explicit import shadows a wildcard import
code: import package::foo::x; import package::other::*; const result = x;

name: wildcard-import-shadow-renamed
desc: an 'as'-renamed import shadows a wildcard import
code: import package::foo::y as x; import package::other::*; const result = x;

name: wildcard-indirect
desc: use a declaration from an outside module, that depends on a wildcard
result: const package_outer_inner_x = 1u; const package_outer_read = package_outer_inner_x; const result = package_outer_read;

name: wildcard-undeclared-ident
desc: fails if the ident does not exist in the wildcard-imported module

name: wildcard-twice-unambiguous
desc: allows two wildcard imports, if there are no ambiguous names used
code: import package::foo::*; import package::bar::*; const z = x + y;

name: wildcard-twice-ambiguous
